newsitem.title: GERMANY: German employer group backs construction pay deal.
newsitem.headline: German employer group backs construction pay deal.

text.p: The German employers' group Bundesvereinigung der Deutschen Arbeitgeberverbaende (BDA) said on Tuesday it was ready under certain conditions to accept a proposed minimum wage deal for construction workers.
One of the main conditions was that the generally binding wage agreement for the industry should only be effective up until May 31, 1997, the BDA said after a meeting of its board.
It added however that new negotiations would have to take place to ensure that the final agreed minimum wage level fitted conditions in comparable sectors.
An earlier agreement on a minimum wage between employers and workers fell apart earlier this year after the BDA vetoed it during early negotiating stages.

The latest agreement was worked out in August and offered west German workers a minimum hourly wage of 17 marks, with their east German colleagues getting 15.64 marks -- in each case lower than the orginal deal.
The wage pact is designed to prevent so-called "wage-dumping" in the sector by foreign companies using cheap labour not bound by German wage deals.
